ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram on the left, the emitter E of transistor T is grounded, the collector C is connected to +U_CC through resistor R_C, and the base B is supplied with base current by +U_CC through bias resistor R_B. On the right are the transistor output characteristic curves, and operating point Q is located on the characteristic curve of I_B = 200 μA. Reasoning: According to the fixed-bias base loop, +U_CC goes through R_B and the base-emitter junction to ground, so the voltage equation of the base loop is U_CC = I_B R_B + U_BE. Substituting U_CC = 20 V, U_BE = 0.6 V, I_B = 200 μA = 200×10^-6 A, gives R_B = (20 - 0.6)/(200×10^-6) = 19.4/0.0002 = 97000 Ω = 97 kΩ.
